cards.meaning: acquittal — the official act of declaring an accused person not guilty
cards.example: Nagdeklara ang Korte Suprema ng pagpapawalang-sala dahil kulang umano ang katunayan na ipinakita ng prosekusyon.
cards.exampleMeaning: The Supreme Court declared an acquittal because the evidence presented by the prosecution was allegedly insufficient.
cards.note: Refers to the legal status itself, distinct from 'pagpapalaya' (the physical act of releasing someone from custody) — a person can be acquitted even if never detained, as in today's case.
cards.tiesTo: Imelda Marcos Supreme Court graft acquittal

cards.meaning: proof; evidence — that which substantiates a claim or accusation
cards.example: Hindi napatunayan ng prosekusyon na tunay at authenticated ang mga dokumentong Swiss, kaya nabuwag ang naunang hatol.
cards.exampleMeaning: The prosecution failed to prove the Swiss documents were genuine and authenticated, so the earlier conviction was overturned.
cards.note: Root is 'tunay' (true/real) — literally names what is verifiably true. 'Sapat na katunayan' (sufficient evidence) is the standard legal-news phrase for the evidentiary bar a conviction must clear.
cards.tiesTo: Imelda Marcos Supreme Court graft acquittal

cards.meaning: in view of; given that — formal connective introducing the reasoning behind an official decision
cards.example: 鉴于监管收紧，越来越多的房企可能被迫违约。
cards.examplePinyin: Jiànyú jiānguǎn shōujǐn, yuèláiyuè duō de fángqǐ kěnéng bèipò wéiyuē.
cards.exampleMeaning: Given the tightening regulatory environment, more and more property developers may be forced into default.
cards.note: Heavily 书面语 (formal/written register) — opens government notices and regulatory filings; distinct from the neutral, register-flexible 因为, which works in any context.

cards.meaning: to default; breach of contract — literally 'violate' + 'agreement,' the formal term for failing to meet a binding obligation
cards.example: 鉴于监管收紧，越来越多的房企可能被迫违约。
cards.examplePinyin: Jiànyú jiānguǎn shōujǐn, yuèláiyuè duō de fángqǐ kěnéng bèipò wéiyuē.
cards.exampleMeaning: Given the tightening regulatory environment, more and more property developers may be forced into default.
cards.note: The formal contractual framing, distinct from casually saying someone 'didn't pay' — carries legal weight and triggers specific consequences under Chinese corporate law; the standard term in China property-debt coverage.
